entry.title: 618 skills, 650 scans, two registries: what a full LLM and meta scan shows
entry.summary: Results from scanning 618 distinct AI agent skills (650 scans) from ClawHub, skills.sh, and major skill repos with every analyzer enabled: 22% flagged, ClawHub far ahead, and most CRITICALs in a handful of security tools.

entry.title: False-positive register
entry.summary: A maintained list of scanner findings on skillscan.io that we believe are wrong, with the reason, so CRITICAL counts can be read with the right discount.

entry.title: Skill Scanner Independently Detected the ClawHavoc Malware Campaign
entry.summary: Koi AI found 341 malicious skills on ClawHub. Cross-referencing our scan results, Cisco's skill-scanner independently detected the same malware campaign — including the same C2 IP address and distribution patterns.

entry.title: First Complete LLM+Meta Scan: 585 Skills Analyzed
entry.summary: After several iterations, API credit exhaustion, and pipeline fixes, we've completed our first clean run with full LLM and meta-analysis. Key insight: LLM analysis catches 83x more social engineering attacks than static analysis.

entry.title: Discovering Silent Pipleine Failures: The LLM Analysis Wasn't Actually Running?!
entry.summary: We discovered that 540 of our scans silently failed to run LLM and meta-analysis due to exhausted API credits. The scanner reported success, but the analysis never happened. Here's how we found the bug and what the real results look like.

entry.title: When the Scanner Scans the Scanner: ClawDefender and the False Positive Problem
entry.summary: ClawDefender, a security skill for OpenClaw agents, was flagged with 37 findings and 22 CRITICAL severity -- making it the highest-finding-count skill in our dataset. Every single finding was a false positive.

entry.title: Exploring Security Testing Capabilities in the AI Agent Skills Ecosystem
entry.summary: AI agent skills execute with full permissions and minimal oversight. An academic study found 26% contain vulnerabilities. We built a prototype automated scanning pipeline to explore the risk landscape.

entry.title: First Scan Results: 22 Skills, 39 Findings
entry.summary: An overview of our initial scan of the top 22 AI agent skills from skills.sh and clawhub.ai, revealing 3 unsafe skills and a dominant data exfiltration pattern.

entry.title: Static-Only vs LLM-Enhanced Scanning
entry.summary: Comparing what static analysis catches versus what Claude Sonnet 4.5 finds -- and why the difference matters for AI agent security.

entry.title: Meta-Analyzer Validation: Reducing False Positives
entry.summary: How the meta-analyzer reviews LLM findings for legitimacy, downgrades false alarms, and adds exploitability context.

entry.title: Scaling to top 50 Skills: New Finding Categories Emerge
entry.summary: Expanding from 22 to 62 (the top 50 from skills.sh plus our prior scans), skills revealed two new threat categories -- prompt injection and tool chaining abuse -- and surfaced browser-use as a high-risk skill class.
